inconsistencies.resolution: Declare one canonical Vietnamese term in §1.1.2 (recommended: "đột quỵ thiếu máu não nhẹ", shortened thereafter to "đột quỵ nhẹ") and one canonical order for the pair, then apply both mechanically to title, headings, captions and body. Fix Bảng 1.3 L137 to "đột quỵ nhẹ có tổn thương vỏ não" so it does not smuggle in a threshold the text rejects.

inconsistencies.what: Diffusion-weighted MRI is rendered five different ways within Chapter 1 and the abbreviation DWI is never defined: "cộng hưởng từ khuếch tán" (L75, L86, Bảng 1.1 L92), "chuỗi xung khuếch tán" (L87, L103, L104), "khuếch tán dương tính" (Bảng 1.3 L131), "tổn thương khuếch tán" (L139), "chuỗi khuếch tán" (Bảng 1.4 L152). Chapter 2 adds "bản đồ hệ số khuếch tán biểu kiến" and "bất tương xứng giữa khuếch tán và FLAIR".
inconsistencies.resolution: Standardise on "cộng hưởng từ khuếch tán (DWI)" at first mention and "DWI" thereafter; add DWI, ADC, FLAIR and SWI to the abbreviation table. Apply the same treatment to "hẹp xơ vữa động mạch nội sọ" / "hẹp nội sọ" / "xơ vữa động mạch nội sọ", used interchangeably at L142, L160 and L167.

inconsistencies.what: Attribution of the ESUS construct is inconsistent. §1.3.2 L148: "năm 2014 Hart và nhóm cộng tác đã đề xuất"; Bảng 1.4 caption L149: "theo Hart và cộng sự [36]"; §2.4.2 L326 and §4.1.1 L564: "Hart và cộng sự". Similarly §1.1.1 L87 names "tuyên bố khoa học do Easton chủ biên" while Bảng 1.1 L97 says "Tuyên bố khoa học AHA (Easton)".
inconsistencies.resolution: Use "và cộng sự" uniformly for all author attributions in running text, and drop author names from table cells (the citation number suffices).

inconsistencies.what: Objective 1 in ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ does not match what Chapter 1 delivers. L80: "1. Cập nhật cơ sở dịch tễ học, định nghĩa, cơ chế bệnh sinh và phân tầng nguy cơ của cơn thiếu máu não thoáng qua và đột quỵ thiếu máu não nhẹ." But risk stratification (ABCD2, ABCD3-I, Canadian TIA Score) is delivered in §2.1.2–2.1.3, not Chapter 1, while two of Chapter 1's five sections — §1.4 (primary prevention, including aspirin, statin, SPRINT, HYVET, PREDIMED, HOPE-3) and §1.5 (TIA clinic model and research role) — are covered by no objective at all.
inconsistencies.locations: L80–L82 (objectives) vs the structure of Chapter 1 (L84–213) and §2.1 (L215–258)
inconsistencies.resolution: Rewrite objective 1 to match: "Hệ thống hoá định nghĩa, dịch tễ học, cơ chế bệnh sinh, yếu tố nguy cơ và vai trò của TIA/đột quỵ nhẹ trong tổ chức phòng ngừa đột quỵ", moving "phân tầng nguy cơ" into objective 2 where ABCD2 actually lives. Alternatively add a fourth objective covering the service-model and Vietnamese-implementation content of §1.5.

inconsistencies.what: The chapter title and two section titles do not describe their content. Chapter 1 is titled "TỔNG QUAN VỀ ĐỘT QUỴ NHẸ VÀ CƠN THIẾU MÁU NÃO THOÁNG QUA" but §1.4.3–1.4.4 is primary-prevention pharmacotherapy overlapping §3.6, and §1.5 is health-service organisation. §1.5 is titled "Vai trò trong nghiên cứu phòng ngừa đột quỵ" — a title with no subject. §1.2.4 is titled "Thực trạng tại Việt Nam và các nước thu nhập trung bình" but its first paragraph (L141) is about global misdiagnosis: "Tỷ lệ TIA bị bỏ sót hoặc chẩn đoán muộn là một vấn đề toàn cầu, được báo cáo từ 9 đến 20%".
inconsistencies.locations: L83 (chapter title), L201 (§1.5 title), L140–141 (§1.2.4 title vs content)
inconsistencies.resolution: Retitle §1.5 to "Vai trò của TIA và đột quỵ nhẹ trong tổ chức phòng ngừa và trong nghiên cứu đột quỵ". Move the global-misdiagnosis paragraph (L141) to §1.1.3 or §1.2.1 and let §1.2.4 be Vietnamese data only. Either retitle §1.4 to "Yếu tố nguy cơ" and relocate the primary-prevention pharmacotherapy, or add "và phòng ngừa tiên phát" to the chapter title.

inconsistencies.what: The 1975 NINDS time-based definition is cited to a source that is not it, and the primary source is absent from the reference list. §1.1.1 L86: "Năm 1975, Uỷ ban Đặc biệt của Viện Quốc gia về Bệnh thần kinh và Đột quỵ Hoa Kỳ định nghĩa TIA là... [7]" — reference [7] is Albers GW et al., "Transient ischemic attack – proposal for a new definition", NEJM 2002. Bảng 1.1 row L97 ("Cơ quan ban hành | Uỷ ban Đặc biệt NINDS") rests on the same wrong citation. The 1975 NINDS Ad Hoc Committee classification appears nowhere in refs 1–130.
inconsistencies.locations: L86 and Bảng 1.1 L97 (§1.1.1); reference [7] in refs.txt
inconsistencies.resolution: Add the primary source (NINDS Ad Hoc Committee, "A classification and outline of cerebrovascular diseases II", Stroke 1975;6:564-616) to the reference list and cite it at L86 and in the Bảng 1.1 caption; keep [7] for the 2002 proposal to abandon the 24-hour rule, which is the correct use of that paper.

inconsistencies.what: Citation ranges bundle primary studies with guidelines and are then used to support guideline claims. ĐVĐ L76: "Các hướng dẫn hiện hành ưu tiên đánh giá bởi chuyên gia trong vòng 24 giờ, chụp cộng hưởng từ khuếch tán khi khả thi... [9-13]" — of refs 9–13 only [12] (ESO 2021) and [13] (AHA 2023) are guidelines; [9] is Johnston 2007 (ABCD2 derivation), [10] Merwick 2010 (ABCD3-I), [11] Coutts 2008 (recurrent-events cohort). The same pattern appears at L74 ("[1-5]"), where [4] and [5] are guidelines and [1]–[3] are prognosis studies.
inconsistencies.resolution: Split composite citations so each clause carries only sources that support it. For guideline statements cite only [4], [5], [12], [13], [18], [41]; keep primary studies for the empirical clauses. This is the detail a Huế examiner checks by sampling three citations at random.

inconsistencies.what: Range punctuation is inconsistent. §1.2.1 L110 uses the word "đến": "dao động từ 50 đến 150 trên 100.000 dân", and L141 likewise "được báo cáo từ 9 đến 20%", while every other range in the chapter uses an en dash ("30–50%", "12–15%", "2–4 lần"). L110 also reads awkwardly: "tăng mạnh theo tuổi và đạt trên 500 trên 100.000 ở nhóm trên 75 tuổi" — three consecutive "trên".
inconsistencies.resolution: Convert all numeric ranges to en dashes ("50–150/100.000 dân", "9–20%") and rewrite L110 as "đạt hơn 500/100.000 dân ở nhóm từ 75 tuổi trở lên".

gaps.missingTopic: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy and transient focal neurological episodes (TFNE, "amyloid spells") as a TIA mimic — and why antithrombotic treatment of them is dangerous
gaps.whyItMatters: The single most consequential omission in the chapter. §1.3.5 covers small-vessel disease as arteriolosclerosis only ("thoái hoá kính – mỡ ở thành tiểu động mạch xuyên") and never mentions CAA, although CAA is the other half of cerebral small-vessel disease and its TFNE — stereotyped, recurrent, spreading positive sensory or negative motor spells lasting minutes — are routinely misdiagnosed as crescendo TIA. Starting DAPT or an anticoagulant in a patient whose "TIA" is convexity subarachnoid haemorrhage or cortical superficial siderosis carries a symptomatic ICH risk of the order of 30–50% over subsequent years. Chapter 2 mentions "bệnh mạch máu não thoái hoá dạng bột" once, in passing, as an SWI indication (L268) — the concept is never introduced, defined or linked to management anywhere. A stroke-neurology examiner will ask about this within the first five minutes.
gaps.whereToAdd: New sub-paragraph in §1.3.5 (after L162), plus a new row in Bảng 1.3 ("Vi xuất huyết thuỳ / xuất huyết dưới nhện lồi não / nhiễm sắt bề mặt vỏ não — chống chỉ định tương đối với kháng kết tập tiểu cầu kép"), plus one clause in the differential sentence at §1.1.3 (L104)

gaps.missingTopic: Haemodynamic (low-flow) TIA, limb-shaking TIA, borderzone infarction and cerebrovascular reserve
gaps.whyItMatters: The candidate's thesis is endovascular treatment of large-vessel occlusion on a background of chronic stenosis — a condition in which the haemodynamic mechanism is central. Yet §1.3.1 disposes of it in a single clause ("hoặc do giảm áp lực tưới máu") and never returns to it, and §1.3.4 treats large-artery atherosclerosis purely as an embolic source. Missing: limb-shaking TIA (rhythmic involuntary limb movements on standing or after antihypertensive dosing, mistaken for focal seizure, with a very high stroke rate and the counter-intuitive rule that lowering blood pressure worsens it), postural and postprandial triggers, internal and cortical borderzone infarct patterns on DWI (rosary-bead pattern), impaired vasomotor reactivity on transcranial Doppler with acetazolamide or breath-holding, and the therapeutic implication that permissive hypertension and volume expansion — not aggressive BP lowering — apply while flow-limiting stenosis persists. This is the natural bridge from Chapter 1 to the thesis.
gaps.whereToAdd: New sub-heading §1.3.4.1, or an expanded second paragraph in §1.3.4 (after L160); plus a Bảng 1.3 row for "triệu chứng khởi phát theo tư thế / sau bữa ăn / sau dùng thuốc hạ áp"

gaps.missingTopic: Capsular warning syndrome and crescendo lacunar TIA
gaps.whyItMatters: §1.3.5 lists Fisher's five lacunar syndromes but omits the one lacunar presentation that is an emergency. Capsular (and pontine) warning syndrome — repeated stereotyped motor or sensorimotor spells over hours without cortical signs — progresses to a completed capsular infarct in roughly 40–60% of cases, the highest short-term risk of any TIA phenotype, and responds poorly to standard antiplatelet therapy. Bảng 1.3 gestures at it ("TIA tái diễn (≥ 2 đợt trong 7 ngày) | Nguy cơ tức thời rất cao, cần nhập viện") without ever naming the syndrome, so a reader cannot recognise it. It also matters for the thesis: stuttering deficits with a fluctuating NIHSS are precisely the presentation of a perforator-territory event on intracranial atherosclerosis.
gaps.whereToAdd: Third paragraph of §1.3.5 (after L162, adjacent to the Fisher syndromes), and rename the Bảng 1.3 row to "TIA tái diễn / hội chứng cảnh báo bao trong"

gaps.missingTopic: Retinal TIA (amaurosis fugax) and central retinal artery occlusion as stroke equivalents
gaps.whyItMatters: The tissue-based definition on which the chapter builds its argument explicitly includes the retina, yet retinal ischaemia gets one clause in §1.1.3 ("thiếu máu võng mạc, mà điển hình là mù thoáng qua một mắt") and one in §2.1.1. Missing entirely: that CRAO carries the same 90-day stroke risk and mandates the identical urgent workup (the AHA 2021 CRAO scientific statement is not in the reference list); that ~25–30% of CRAO patients have significant ipsilateral carotid stenosis and a further ~10% have AF; the distinction between non-arteritic CRAO and giant cell arteritis (jaw claudication, scalp tenderness, ESR/CRP, temporal artery biopsy, immediate high-dose steroids to save the fellow eye); the futility of ocular massage and anterior-chamber paracentesis; and the fact that painless monocular visual loss is routinely routed to ophthalmology rather than to a stroke pathway. In Vietnam that misrouting is near-universal and is a concrete implementation point the monograph should own.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §1.1.4 "Thiếu máu võng mạc thoáng qua và tắc động mạch trung tâm võng mạc" (after L105), or an expanded item (iii) of §1.1.3

gaps.missingTopic: Substantive Vietnamese epidemiological and health-system data
gaps.whyItMatters: §1.2.4 and §1.5.4 together run ~600 words about Vietnam and contain not a single Vietnamese number. The chapter says "Số liệu Việt Nam chưa đầy đủ" and "Mạng lưới đơn vị đột quỵ đã phát triển nhanh trong thập niên gần đây nhưng vẫn phân bố không đồng đều" — both unquantified, both citing [21] and [34], which hold the data the text declines to report. A Huế committee will expect: national stroke incidence and mortality from GBD 1990–2021; mean age at onset in Vietnam versus high-income countries; the number and geographic distribution of certified stroke units and the population per centre; RES-Q process indicators (door-to-needle, proportion receiving vascular imaging, proportion discharged on antithrombotics); MRI and CT-angiography availability by hospital tier; BHYT coverage status for clopidogrel, ticagrelor, DOACs, CTA and MRI; median presentation delay; and the near-absence of any TIA-specific pathway. Without these, the "định hướng triển khai" section is aspiration rather than analysis.
gaps.whereToAdd: Rewrite §1.2.4 (L140–142) around a new table "Bảng 1.7. Một số chỉ số dịch tễ và tổ chức chăm sóc đột quỵ tại Việt Nam"

gaps.missingTopic: Cost-effectiveness of the rapid TIA clinic model, with a Vietnamese cost frame
gaps.whyItMatters: §1.5 argues for the TIA-clinic model entirely on efficacy. The only economic statement in the chapter is the throwaway "không tăng chi phí toàn phần" (L208). Missing: the EXPRESS economic analysis (urgent assessment reduced total costs by shortening admissions), cost per stroke averted and per QALY, the NICE/HAS positions, and — decisively for this monograph — an estimate for Vietnam built from actual BHYT tariffs: the cost of same-day MRI with DWI, CTA head-neck, echocardiography, 24h Holter and 21 days of clopidogrel plus aspirin, versus the cost of one admitted moderate-to-severe stroke with rehabilitation. This is the argument that persuades a Vietnamese hospital director, and the argument a committee will ask the candidate to make.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §1.5.5 "Chi phí – hiệu quả của mô hình phòng khám TIA và khả năng áp dụng tại Việt Nam", or a substantial expansion of §1.5.4 (L213)

gaps.missingTopic: Quality indicators and KPIs for a TIA service
gaps.whyItMatters: §1.5.1 lists the clinic's "đặc trưng cốt lõi" as a prose list of activities (L204) but supplies no measurable indicators, so the model cannot be audited or improved. A monograph at this level should specify: proportion assessed by a stroke specialist within 24 hours; door-to-DWI and door-to-vascular-imaging times; proportion started on antithrombotic therapy on the day of assessment; proportion with AF anticoagulated at discharge; proportion with symptomatic carotid stenosis revascularised within 14 days; LDL-C target attainment at 3 months; 90-day recurrent stroke rate; mimic rate (a quality signal in both directions); loss to follow-up; and adherence at 12 months. These map directly onto the RES-Q registry in which Vietnam already participates — cited at [34] but never used.
gaps.whereToAdd: New table in §1.5.4 ("Bảng 1.8. Bộ chỉ số chất lượng đề xuất cho phòng khám TIA") plus a short interpretive paragraph

gaps.missingTopic: Telemedicine and tele-TIA pathways
gaps.whyItMatters: Telemedicine appears exactly once in Chapter 1 — buried inside the Hình 1.2 caption ("được hẹn khám trực tiếp hoặc khám từ xa trong cùng ngày") — and once more at §4.4.2. It is never discussed in the body. Reference [51] (Wechsler et al., "Evaluation of transient ischemic attack and minor stroke: a rapid outpatient model for the COVID-19 pandemic and beyond") is precisely a paper about this and is used only for a figure caption. For Vietnam, where the specialist workforce is concentrated in Hà Nội, Huế and Hồ Chí Minh City while most TIA patients present to district hospitals, a tele-TIA triage pathway is arguably the highest-yield implementation proposal the monograph could make: video-based history and examination, remote NIHSS, store-and-forward CT/CTA review, teleconsultation-driven decisions on admission versus same-day outpatient workup, and the medico-legal and reimbursement framework under Vietnam's telehealth regulations.
gaps.whereToAdd: New paragraph in §1.5.1 (after L204) and a corresponding implementation direction in §1.5.4 (L213), which currently lists four directions and should list five

gaps.missingTopic: Patient education, return to driving and return to work after TIA/minor stroke
gaps.whyItMatters: Absent from the entire monograph apart from a single functional-assessment clause at §1.1.2 ("khả năng trở lại công việc"). §1.5.4 mentions "giáo dục cộng đồng" but nothing about educating the individual patient. Every TIA patient discharged from a clinic must be told: the warning symptoms mandating immediate return (calling 115), that a further event is most likely within 48 hours, what each medication does and that DAPT stops on a defined date, and the driving restriction — typically no private driving for one month after TIA or minor stroke with full recovery, longer and formally assessed for commercial licences, with the Vietnamese rules under the Thông tư on driver health standards stated explicitly. Return-to-work advice and recognition of post-stroke fatigue and vascular cognitive impairment in "minor" patients belong here too. The absence is visible because this is a standard component of every published TIA-clinic protocol.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §1.5.5 or a dedicated paragraph in §1.5.4 (after L213); a short cross-reference from the disability discussion at §1.1.2 (L100)

gaps.missingTopic: Stroke in the young, pregnancy and the puerperium, and hormonal exposure
gaps.whyItMatters: §1.3.5 mentions dissection "ở người trẻ dưới 55 tuổi" and lists inherited thrombophilias, but there is no treatment of young stroke as an entity — despite 10–15% of ischaemic strokes occurring under 50 and the incidence rising, and despite Vietnam's younger mean age at onset being one of the chapter's own claims (L142). Missing: the young-stroke differential (dissection, PFO, RCVS, cardiac including endocarditis and myxoma, vasculitis, Fabry, MELAS, moyamoya, substance use — methamphetamine use is a growing Vietnamese problem); pregnancy and post-partum stroke (pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, RCVS, cerebral venous thrombosis, peripartum cardiomyopathy) and the fact that thrombolysis and thrombectomy are not absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy; and combined oral contraceptive risk, amplified by smoking and migraine with aura. §2.1.1 asks the clinician to record "thuốc tránh thai... và liệu pháp hormone" without the chapter ever explaining why.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §1.3.6 "Đột quỵ ở người trẻ, thai kỳ và hậu sản" (after L163), with a matching row in §1.4.2 (non-modifiable and sex-specific factors, L179)

gaps.missingTopic: Hypercoagulability and cancer-associated stroke workup
gaps.whyItMatters: §1.3.5 lists inherited thrombophilias in one sentence ("yếu tố V Leiden, đột biến prothrombin G20210A, thiếu hụt protein C, protein S hoặc antithrombin") in a way that implies they are relevant causes of arterial stroke — the opposite of current understanding, and §2.4.2 correctly warns against routine thrombophilia panels ("Xét nghiệm tăng đông không nên thực hiện như một bộ xét nghiệm thường quy"). Chapter 1 must set that up rather than contradict it. Missing: that inherited thrombophilias are venous rather than arterial risk factors and matter chiefly via paradoxical embolism through a PFO; antiphospholipid syndrome as the exception, with the 2023 ACR/EULAR classification criteria, the requirement for repeat testing at 12 weeks, and the fact that the acute phase and concurrent anticoagulation invalidate several assays; and cancer-associated stroke (Trousseau syndrome, non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis, elevated D-dimer, multi-territory DWI lesions crossing vascular territories, adenocarcinoma of lung/pancreas/stomach, LMWH preferred over DOAC acutely) — which Chapter 2 (L318) and Chapter 4 (L566) both invoke without Chapter 1 ever establishing the mechanism.
gaps.whereToAdd: Expanded second paragraph of §1.3.5 (L163), replacing the current bare list

gaps.missingTopic: Burden of disease beyond recurrent stroke — disability, cognition, mood, work and cost after a "minor" event
gaps.whyItMatters: §1.2 is titled "Dịch tễ học và gánh nặng bệnh tật" but quantifies only recurrent stroke risk; "gánh nặng bệnh tật" is never delivered. Missing: that 20–40% of NIHSS ≤5 patients are not functionally independent (mRS ≥2) at 90 days despite the "minor" label — the strongest possible support for the chapter's own argument at §1.1.2 that a low NIHSS is not a benign event; post-TIA and post-minor-stroke cognitive impairment and elevated dementia risk; anxiety, depression and post-event PTSD; return-to-work rates; and the economic burden (direct costs, productivity loss, caregiver burden), which is what makes the cost-effectiveness case in §1.5. Chapter 3 mentions MoCA screening and post-stroke depression at 30–40% (L558, L537) — figures that belong first in Chapter 1's burden section.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §1.2.5 "Gánh nặng chức năng, nhận thức và kinh tế" (after L139)

gaps.missingTopic: Explicit link between this monograph and the doctoral thesis on endovascular treatment of LVO on chronic intracranial stenosis
gaps.whyItMatters: Objective 3 promises "định hướng nghiên cứu có liên quan đến đề tài luận án" (L82), but neither ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ nor Chapter 1 ever explains the connection, and the reader reaches the end of Chapter 1 without knowing why a candidate studying ICAS-LVO thrombectomy wrote a monograph on TIA. The link is strong and should be stated: TIA and minor stroke are the pre-event phase of ICAS-related LVO; patients with intracranial atherosclerosis characteristically present with fluctuating, stuttering, low-NIHSS deficits before occluding, so the population Chapter 1 describes is the one that later fills the thrombectomy suite; the DAPT and high-intensity statin decisions analysed in Chapter 3 are the same decisions made periprocedurally for rescue stenting; and CYP2C19 genotype, treated in Chapter 3 as a secondary-prevention issue, governs stent thrombosis risk. Without this paragraph the monograph reads as unrelated to the thesis — the most visible structural weakness for a committee.
gaps.whereToAdd: A new sixth paragraph in ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ (between L78 and L79) and a closing paragraph in §1.5.4 (after L213)

gaps.missingTopic: Comparison of the Bộ Y tế 2024 guideline against AHA/ASA and ESO on TIA definition, urgency, imaging and DAPT
gaps.whyItMatters: Reference [4] (Quyết định 3312/QĐ-BYT) is cited five times in Chapter 1 but the chapter never states what it actually says beyond the NIHSS ≤5 threshold. For a Vietnamese doctoral monograph whose stated purpose (L78) is "đối chiếu với hướng dẫn của Bộ Y tế và đề xuất quy trình khả thi cho điều kiện Việt Nam", this is the central analytical task and it is skipped. A side-by-side comparison is needed on: the TIA definition adopted; whether specialist assessment within 24 hours is mandated; whether DWI is recommended and within what window; vascular imaging requirements; DAPT indication, drug, loading dose and duration; anticoagulation timing after AF-related infarct; and carotid revascularisation timing. Where Bộ Y tế is silent or differs, the monograph should say so and propose a defensible local position.
gaps.whereToAdd: New table and interpretive paragraph in §1.1.2 (after L101), or at the head of §1.5.4

gaps.missingTopic: Under-recognised primary-prevention risk factors relevant to Vietnam
gaps.whyItMatters: §1.4.1 covers the classic six and Bảng 1.6 adds obesity, inactivity and diet, but several factors with strong evidence and direct Vietnamese relevance are absent from Chapter 1: chronic kidney disease; obstructive sleep apnoea (which appears only in Bảng 3.10, secondary prevention); migraine with aura, particularly combined with smoking and combined oral contraceptives in young women; residual inflammatory risk and hsCRP (colchicine surfaces only once, in §4.3, as CHANCE-3); air pollution, a leading INTERSTROKE-identified factor and a major Vietnamese urban exposure; psychosocial stress; and heavy episodic alcohol use. Vietnamese-specific quantification is also missing: adult male smoking prevalence around 40%, mean dietary sodium intake of roughly 9–10 g/day against the <5 g target the chapter itself states in Bảng 1.6, and low hypertension treatment and control rates. The polypill/fixed-dose combination strategy for primary prevention in resource-limited settings is likewise absent.
gaps.whereToAdd: Expanded §1.4.1 (L176–177) with 2–3 new rows in Bảng 1.6, plus a Vietnamese-prevalence sentence per major factor

gaps.missingTopic: NIHSS item-level structure and which deficits the scale under-weights
gaps.whyItMatters: §1.1.2 builds its entire argument on the NIHSS — the ≤3 versus ≤5 threshold problem and the claim that "'nhẹ' theo thang NIHSS không đồng nghĩa với 'không gây tàn tật'" — yet the reader is never shown what the scale measures. The argument only lands if item-level weighting is visible: visual fields maximum 3, limb ataxia maximum 2 (and scored 0 when the limb is plegic), extinction/inattention maximum 2, language maximum 3, and no item at all for hand dexterity, gait or diplopia. That is why a patient with an isolated dominant-hand deficit or a hemianopia can score 1–2 and still be unable to work or drive. The full 15-item table belongs in §2.1.4, but Chapter 1 needs the underweighted-items point made concretely with maxima rather than as the current unquantified list at L100.
gaps.whereToAdd: One paragraph in §1.1.2 (after L100) naming the under-weighted items with their maximum scores, with a forward reference to the full item table that should be added at §2.1.4

gaps.missingTopic: ABCD2 failure in the posterior circulation
gaps.whyItMatters: The chapter's own Bảng 1.3 makes ABCD2 ≥4 the leading high-risk marker, and ĐVĐ warns generically that a low score can hide high-risk mechanisms — but nowhere does the document explain the specific and predictable failure mode: vertebrobasilar TIA typically produces vertigo, diplopia, dysarthria or ataxia rather than unilateral weakness or speech disturbance, so it scores 0 on the clinical component and often 0–2 overall despite carrying a substantial risk of basilar occlusion. Posterior-circulation events also show higher early recurrence and are more often DWI-negative on early imaging. The full treatment belongs at §2.1.3, but Chapter 1's risk-stratification table must not present ABCD2 without this caveat attached.
gaps.whereToAdd: One sentence in §1.2.3 (L126) plus a new Bảng 1.3 row ("Triệu chứng thuộc hệ tuần hoàn sau — ABCD2 đánh giá thấp một cách hệ thống"); the fuller discussion (~350 words) belongs to the Chapter 2 reviewer at §2.1.3

gaps.missingTopic: A statement of review methodology and evidence cut-off
gaps.whyItMatters: ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ ends with three objectives and no account of how the literature was assembled. A chuyên đề scored 9–10 should state the databases searched (PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane, Embase), the keyword strategy, the date range, the guideline versions adopted (Bộ Y tế 2024, AHA/ASA 2021 secondary prevention and 2026 acute management, ESO 2021 TIA and 2024 PFO), the inclusion hierarchy (guidelines and randomised evidence over observational data), and the evidence cut-off. That cut-off currently appears exactly once, deep in §4.4.1 ("tính đến tháng 8 năm 2026"), where no reader will find it.
gaps.whereToAdd: A short methods paragraph at the end of ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ, between L79 and L80, or immediately after the objectives at L82

gaps.missingTopic: Breakthrough events on antithrombotic therapy, and the service pathway for them
gaps.whyItMatters: §1.5.1's list of core clinic features (L204) covers triage, imaging, cardiac workup and follow-up, but not the commonest difficult case in a real TIA clinic: the patient who has an event while already on aspirin, clopidogrel, DAPT or a DOAC. That patient needs adherence verification, re-examination of the mechanism (a breakthrough event usually means a missed mechanism rather than aspirin failure), a check for drug interaction and CYP2C19 status, and a decision on switching versus escalating — not a reflex change of agent. Chapter 3 touches this once (L403) but the service-design implication belongs to §1.5. Perioperative and periprocedural antithrombotic management, DOAC renal dosing and reversal agents are properly Chapter 3 topics and should be flagged to that reviewer, but §1.4.3 introduces DOAC preference (L197) with no dosing or renal caveat at all, which needs at minimum a forward reference.
gaps.whereToAdd: One bullet added to the core-features list in §1.5.1 (L204); one clause plus a forward reference to §3.4 at §1.4.3 (L197)

formattingIssues: Cross-reference error, Hình 1.1 (L105–107): the "(Hình 1.1)" call-out is attached to a sentence about the 80% risk reduction from rapid TIA clinics, but the figure shows the TIA/acute-coronary-syndrome analogy and the tissue-versus-time concept. Move the call-out to §1.1.1 (L86–87), where that contrast is actually made, or reword the sentence at L105.

Caption style, Hình 1.2 (L206): the caption runs ~110 words and narrates an entire flowchart in prose ("người bệnh gọi điện, điều dưỡng phân loại theo bảng kiểm tiêu chuẩn — không đạt tiêu chuẩn thì chuyển khoa cấp cứu; nếu đạt, được hẹn khám trực tiếp hoặc khám từ xa..."). Cut to one sentence naming what the figure shows, and move the pathway description into the body of §1.5.1, where it is needed anyway.

Unverifiable label in the Hình 1.2 caption: the flowchart is called "quy trình RESCUE-TIA", a name appearing nowhere else in the monograph and not the name of the model described in reference [51] (Wechsler et al., a rapid outpatient model). Either source the name or delete it — an examiner will read it as a trial acronym.

Source-line convention used exactly once in the whole document: Hình 2.5 carries a separate "<Normal> Nguồn: Ntaios và cộng sự [37]; tiêu chí gốc theo Hart và cộng sự [36]." line, whereas every other figure and table embeds its citation in the caption. Pick one convention and apply it to Hình 1.1 and Hình 1.2.

Bảng 1.4 (L149–156) is not a table: column 1 contains only "1, 2, 3, 4" and column 2 contains four long sentences duplicating the paragraph immediately above it (L148). Convert to a numbered list, or add columns that earn the space ("Cách xác định trên thực hành", "Khảo sát tối thiểu để khẳng định") — and see the redundancy note recommending it move to Chapter 4 entirely.

Bảng 1.3 column 3 is heterogeneous: the header reads "Cơ sở bằng chứng / nguy cơ tương đối" but the cells mix absolute 90-day risks ("8–11% so với 1–3%"), fold-increases ("tăng 2–4 lần"), an absolute annual risk ("khoảng 12%/năm"), a qualitative comparison ("Nguy cơ cao hơn so với chỉ rối loạn cảm giác hoặc thị giác") and a scoring rule that is not a risk at all ("Yếu tố trong thang ABCD2 (2 điểm)"). Split into "Ước lượng nguy cơ" and "Nguồn", and give every row the same metric type.

Bảng 1.6 caption (L182) announces "nguy cơ tương đối và mục tiêu kiểm soát" but the table has a fourth column, "Mức khuyến cáo", that the caption does not mention. Worse, the class of recommendation is attached to the risk factor rather than to an action — a Class I recommendation applies to an intervention, not to "Tăng huyết áp". Retitle the column "Mức khuyến cáo của can thiệp tương ứng" and update the caption.
Table placement versus call-out: Bảng 1.6 duplicates §1.4.1's prose (L176) but is called out from §1.4.3 (L181), two subsections later. Move the call-out to L176.

Bảng 1.5 (L165–172): the five percentage estimates sum to 75–105%, and the row labelled "Lấp mạch chưa rõ nguồn" mixes the ESUS construct into a TOAST-style aetiological taxonomy. Rescale, relabel, and add a caption footnote stating that the ranges come from mixed cohorts and do not sum to 100%.

Bảng 1.5 column 4 ("Phòng ngừa thứ phát") imports Chapter 3 content into a Chapter 1 aetiology table with no cross-reference in either direction. Either delete the column or append "(chi tiết ở Mục 3.2–3.5)" to the caption.
No table in Chapter 1 carries a footnote or abbreviation key, although the tables use NIHSS, ABCD2, DASH, BMI, SGLT-2, GLP-1, CHA2DS2-VASc and LDL-C. Add a standard footnote line under each table.

The abbreviation table (L59–72) has 18 entries and no header row ("Chữ viết tắt | Nội dung"). It omits terms used in Chapter 1 — DWI, AHA/ASA, ESO, LDL-C, HDL-C, BMI, HbA1c, NT-proBNP, GBD, RES-Q, CICAS, SGLT-2, GLP-1, NOTCH3, ApoE4, RNF213 — and, from later chapters, FLAIR, SWI, PFO, DOAC, INR, PHQ-9, SSRI, PCSK9. The NASCET entry also carries an explanatory clause ("— cũng chỉ phương pháp đo mức hẹp tương ứng") that no other entry has; move that explanation to §3.5.1.

Front matter is incomplete: there is no DANH MỤC BẢNG and no DANH MỤC HÌNH, although the monograph contains 27 tables and at least 12 figures; and MỤC LỤC does not list DANH MỤC CÁC CHỮ VIẾT TẮT even though that section exists (L58).

MỤC LỤC lists only levels 1 and 2 while the body uses level-3 headings throughout (1.1.1, 1.1.2, …). For a document of this length, either include level 3 in the contents or state the depth convention.

MỤC LỤC/heading mismatch: the contents entry "4.4. Định hướng nghiên cứu và liên hệ với luận án" (L52) versus the body heading "4.4. Định hướng nghiên cứu" (L650). Regenerate the contents from the body.

Uncited references: [56] (Sehatzadeh, "Is transient ischemic attack a medical emergency?"), [69] and [111] appear in the reference list but are cited nowhere in the body. [56] belongs in §1.1.3 or §1.5.1 and would let one of the repeated "TIA is an emergency" assertions be replaced by a proper citation; the other two must be cited or removed.

Missing primary reference: the 1975 NINDS Ad Hoc Committee classification, on which §1.1.1 (L86) and Bảng 1.1 (L97) both rest, is not in the reference list; the claim is currently carried by [7], which is Albers 2002.

Caption punctuation is inconsistent across the document: Chapter 1 captions end with a citation followed by a full stop ("...[6-8]."), while Bảng 4.3 (L607), for example, ends "[125]" with no full stop. Standardise.

Chapter 1 uses no forward cross-references although it repeatedly states material developed later (ESUS criteria, DAPT durations, carotid revascularisation thresholds, AF monitoring yields). Chapter 3 does use them ("Quản lý lipid theo Mục 3.3", L535). Adopt one convention — "xem Mục x.y" — and apply it in Chapter 1, which would simultaneously resolve several of the redundancies above.

The objectives at L80–L82 are typed as ordinary paragraphs beginning "1.", "2.", "3." rather than as a numbered list style, so the template will not pick them up consistently. Also, three objectives are mapped onto four chapters, with objective 3 silently covering both Chapter 3 and Chapter 4; either add a fourth objective or state the mapping explicitly.

Subsection weight is uneven in §1.3: §1.3.1, §1.3.3 and §1.3.4 are each a single paragraph under a level-3 heading, while §1.3.5 carries two paragraphs plus a table. Either merge the single-paragraph subsections or expand them (the gaps list supplies the material for §1.3.4 and §1.3.5).

Range punctuation is inconsistent: L110 and L141 use the word "đến" ("từ 50 đến 150 trên 100.000 dân", "từ 9 đến 20%") while every other range in the chapter uses an en dash. L110 also repeats "trên" three times in one clause ("đạt trên 500 trên 100.000 ở nhóm trên 75 tuổi").

redundancies.what: Toàn bộ nội dung tiêu sợi huyết trong §2.1.4 lặp lại §3.1.2 gần như nguyên văn. §2.1.4: "Hướng dẫn năm 2026 của Hiệp hội Tim mạch và Đột quỵ Hoa Kỳ đề nghị tiêu sợi huyết đường tĩnh mạch trong cửa sổ 4,5 giờ cho mọi thiếu sót gây tàn tật, bất kể điểm NIHSS... alteplase 0,9 mg/kg hoặc tenecteplase 0,25 mg/kg với liều tối đa 25 mg là các lựa chọn được khuyến cáo. Ngược lại, ở thiếu sót nhẹ không gây tàn tật trong cửa sổ 4,5 giờ, tiêu sợi huyết không mang lại lợi ích và kháng kết tập tiểu cầu kép được ưu tiên nếu nguyên nhân không phải từ tim." §3.1.2: "...hướng dẫn năm 2026 khuyến cáo tiêu sợi huyết đường tĩnh mạch sau khi loại trừ chống chỉ định, bất kể điểm NIHSS; tenecteplase 0,25 mg/kg với liều tối đa 25 mg hoặc alteplase 0,9 mg/kg là các lựa chọn. Ở thiếu sót nhẹ không gây tàn tật, tiêu sợi huyết không mang lại lợi ích và kháng kết tập tiểu cầu kép được ưu tiên nếu nguyên nhân không phải từ tim." The second sentence is word-for-word identical. Both cite [5,59,60].
redundancies.locations: §2.1.4 (lines 255–256) vs §3.1.2 (line 375); same drug doses also repeated in ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ ¶4
redundancies.recommendation: A diagnosis chapter must not carry treatment indications. Cut the two therapeutic sentences and the drug doses from §2.1.4 entirely; keep only the diagnostic act — how to elicit and document a disabling deficit — and end with a cross-reference "quyết định tái tưới máu được trình bày tại Mục 3.1.2". This alone removes ~180 redundant words and repairs the chapter's scope.

redundancies.what: §2.3.4 ¶2 restates the anticoagulation indication and DOAC-vs-VKA choice already given in §3.4.1 ¶1. §2.3.4: "...tiền sử biến cố đã cho 2 điểm trong thang CHA2DS2-VASc và thường tạo chỉ định kháng đông nếu không có chống chỉ định. Thuốc kháng đông đường uống trực tiếp được ưu tiên hơn kháng vitamin K trong rung nhĩ không kèm van cơ học hoặc hẹp van hai lá mức trung bình đến nặng; liều phải được điều chỉnh theo tuổi, cân nặng, chức năng thận và tương tác thuốc [18]." §3.4.1: "...tiền sử TIA hoặc đột quỵ đã tạo 2 điểm trong thang CHA2DS2-VASc nên đa số người bệnh có chỉ định kháng đông... Thuốc kháng đông đường uống trực tiếp được ưu tiên trong rung nhĩ không kèm van cơ học hoặc hẹp van hai lá mức trung bình đến nặng, với liều điều chỉnh theo chức năng thận, tuổi, cân nặng và tương tác thuốc [18,66-68]."
redundancies.recommendation: Delete §2.3.4 ¶2 and replace with a single clause at the end of ¶1: "...việc xác nhận rung nhĩ làm thay đổi chiến lược phòng ngừa thứ phát (Mục 3.4)". The half-stated dose-adjustment sentence is worse than useless in Ch.2 because no dosing table follows it anywhere in the monograph (see gap on DOAC dosing).

redundancies.what: Section 2.4 ("Phân loại nguyên nhân", ~1,135 words) largely re-derives §1.3.2–1.3.5. The five TOAST subtypes with percentages appear in §1.3.2, in Bảng 1.5, and again in §2.4.1 ("xơ vữa động mạch lớn chiếm 15–25%; lấp mạch nguồn tim chiếm 20–30%; bệnh mạch máu nhỏ... khoảng 25%..."). The four ESUS criteria appear five times in the monograph: §1.3.2 prose, Bảng 1.4 (item-by-item), §2.4.2 prose ("tổn thương lấp mạch không phải dạng ổ khuyết...; không có hẹp từ 50% trở lên...; không có nguồn lấp mạch tim nguy cơ cao...; và không có nguyên nhân xác định khác"), Bảng 2.5, and §4.1.1.
redundancies.recommendation: Highest-yield structural fix in the chapter. Delete the prose restatement of TOAST subtypes and of the four ESUS criteria from §2.4.1–2.4.2 (cross-refer to Bảng 1.4/1.5). Rebuild §2.4 as what a diagnosis chapter actually needs and the monograph currently lacks: an operational bedside algorithm for assigning a subtype — the minimum dataset, the rule for competing causes, confidence grading (CCS levels), and what to do when the workup is incomplete. Keep only Bảng 2.5 as the TOAST-vs-ESUS comparison. Net saving ~450 words, freeing space for the hypercoagulability/young-stroke gaps below.

redundancies.what: The East-Asian intracranial atherosclerosis block in §2.4.4 duplicates §1.3.4 and §1.2.4 in content, figures and conclusion. §1.3.4: "hẹp xơ vữa động mạch nội sọ chiếm 30–50% tại các quần thể Đông Á..., theo nghiên cứu CICAS. Sự khác biệt về phân bố giải phẫu này có ý nghĩa quan trọng cho cả chiến lược chẩn đoán hình ảnh mạch máu — ưu tiên khảo sát toàn trục mạch máu ở quần thể châu Á — lẫn lựa chọn điều trị..." §2.4.4: "...hẹp xơ vữa động mạch nội sọ là nguyên nhân chính của nhóm xơ vữa động mạch lớn ở Đông Á, chiếm tới 30–50% số ca nhồi máu não... cần ưu tiên khảo sát toàn bộ cây mạch máu nội sọ bằng chụp mạch cắt lớp vi tính hoặc cộng hưởng từ, và cân nhắc sớm kháng kết tập tiểu cầu kép cường độ cao..." The imaging consequence is stated a third time in §2.2.3 and a fourth in §2.2.4 (tầng một/tầng ba).
redundancies.locations: §2.4.4 (line 344) vs §1.3.4 (line 160) vs §1.2.4 (line 142); imaging consequence also §2.2.3 (line 270) and §2.2.4 (line 288)
redundancies.recommendation: Keep the epidemiology in §1.3.4 only. In §2.4.4 retain a single sentence of diagnostic consequence and delete the therapeutic clause ("cân nhắc sớm kháng kết tập tiểu cầu kép cường độ cao... theo bằng chứng từ SAMMPRIS, CHANCE và POINT"), which duplicates §3.2.2 and §3.5.3 and is also inconsistent with them (see inconsistency on the 70–99% threshold).

redundancies.what: The "TIA clinic reduces 90-day recurrence by 80%" claim is made five times. §2.5.4 (final sentence of Chương 2): "Mô hình đánh giá nhanh tại các phòng khám TIA chuyên khoa đã chứng minh giảm 80% nguy cơ đột quỵ 90 ngày so với chăm sóc thường quy..." Identical claims in ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ ¶5 ("giảm khoảng 80% nguy cơ đột quỵ tái phát trong 90 ngày"), §1.1.3 ("giảm tới 80%"), §1.2.2 (EXPRESS 10,3% → 2,1%, "khoảng 80%"), §1.5.2, and Bảng 4.4 row "Mô hình phòng khám nhanh | EXPRESS, SOS-TIA | 2007 | Đánh giá khẩn cấp giảm 80% tái phát trong 90 ngày".
redundancies.recommendation: In §2.5.4 the 80% figure is off-topic — the subsection is about missed strokes and misdiagnosis. Replace the closing sentence with the diagnostic-accuracy point that actually belongs there (mimic rate and inter-rater reliability of the TIA diagnosis) and drop the efficacy claim.

redundancies.what: The warning that early DWI can be falsely negative, especially for small or posterior-circulation lesions, is made three times inside Chương 2. §2.2.1: "chuỗi xung khuếch tán chụp sớm có thể âm tính, nhất là với ổ nhỏ hoặc tổn thương tuần hoàn sau, nên kết quả âm tính không loại trừ thiếu máu não..." §2.2.2: "Độ nhạy đối với ổ thiếu máu rất sớm, ổ nhỏ hoặc tổn thương tuần hoàn sau thấp hơn cộng hưởng từ khuếch tán..." §2.5.4: "...lưu ý cộng hưởng từ chụp rất sớm có thể âm tính giả ở tuần hoàn sau." §2.5.3 adds a fourth variant: "kết quả âm tính không loại trừ TIA hay đột quỵ nhẹ".
redundancies.recommendation: State it once, in §2.2.1, with the quantitative anchor missing everywhere (repeat-DWI positivity rises when imaging is performed 24–72 h after onset). Convert the other three into a cross-reference.

redundancies.what: The Calvet et al. finding is stated twice in near-identical wording. §1.2.3: "Calvet và cộng sự đã chứng minh rằng phối hợp hai yếu tố này cải thiện đáng kể khả năng tiên đoán đột quỵ tái phát so với chỉ dùng ABCD2..." §2.2.1: "Calvet và cộng sự đã chứng minh rằng chuỗi xung khuếch tán dương tính cộng với nguyên nhân động mạch lớn cải thiện đáng kể khả năng tiên đoán đột quỵ tái phát so với chỉ dùng ABCD2 đơn thuần." Citation also drifts ([32,33] in Ch.1, [32] in Ch.2).
redundancies.recommendation: Keep in §2.2.1 (where imaging is the subject) with the effect size (c-statistic improvement) actually quoted; in §1.2.3 reduce to a table row in Bảng 1.3, which already carries both predictors.

redundancies.what: The "do not use ABCD2 alone" caution is repeated four times. ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ ¶3: "ABCD2 không phải là công cụ chẩn đoán và không được dùng đơn độc để quyết định cho xuất viện, nhập viện hay trì hoãn khảo sát: điểm thấp vẫn có thể che giấu hẹp động mạch có triệu chứng hoặc nguồn lấp mạch từ tim." §2.1.3: "...không dùng điểm số đơn độc để xác định người bệnh 'nguy cơ thấp', để quyết định cho xuất viện hay để trì hoãn đánh giá; điểm ABCD2 từ 3 trở xuống vẫn có thể che giấu hẹp động mạch có triệu chứng, nhiều cơn tái diễn hoặc cơ chế nguồn tim." Repeated again in §3.1.1, in §3.1.3 ("Không dùng ABCD2 đơn độc để quyết định nơi chăm sóc") and as a row of Bảng 3.1.
redundancies.recommendation: §2.1.3 is the correct canonical home. Delete the sentence from ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ and from §3.1.1, leaving only the Bảng 3.1 row and a cross-reference to §2.1.3.

redundancies.what: The ABCD2 components are rendered three times within thirty lines: in prose (§2.1.2 ¶1), in Bảng 2.1 rows 2–6, and again in the caption of Hình 2.1, which re-lists every item with its points: "tuổi từ 60 trở lên (1 điểm); huyết áp tâm thu từ 140 mmHg trở lên hoặc tâm trương từ 90 mmHg trở lên (1 điểm); liệt một bên (2 điểm) hoặc rối loạn ngôn ngữ không kèm liệt (1 điểm); thời gian triệu chứng từ 60 phút trở lên (2 điểm) hoặc 10–59 phút (1 điểm); và đái tháo đường (1 điểm)".
redundancies.recommendation: Keep Bảng 2.1 as the authoritative rendering. Either delete Hình 2.1 (it carries no information the table lacks) or, better, replace it with the figure the chapter genuinely needs — a decision flow of the first 24 hours, or the NIHSS item card. Shorten the caption to one line.

redundancies.what: Vascular-territory syndromes are described twice within §2.1. §2.1.1 ¶2: "liệt mặt, liệt nửa người ở tay hoặc chân, mất ngôn ngữ kiểu Broca, Wernicke hoặc toàn bộ, mù thoáng qua một mắt gợi ý hệ động mạch cảnh trong; ngược lại, chóng mặt phối hợp với song thị, nuốt khó, yếu tứ chi và thất điều gợi ý hệ tuần hoàn sau." §2.1.5: "Hội chứng động mạch cảnh trong gồm liệt nửa người ưu thế tay – mặt, mất thị trường cùng bên, mất ngôn ngữ kiểu Broca hoặc Wernicke..., và mù thoáng qua một mắt cùng bên hẹp... Hội chứng tuần hoàn sau gồm chóng mặt, song thị, nuốt khó, thất điều..." Both cite [6,22].
redundancies.recommendation: Merge into a single unit and move it up to sit immediately after §2.1.1 (the history/exam subsection), so the chapter flows history → exam → territorial syndromes → risk scores → disabling-deficit assessment. In §2.1.1 keep only the history-taking instruction (timing, triggers, medications), not the symptom lists.

redundancies.what: The atrial cardiopathy biomarker triad is stated three times inside Chương 2 and twice more elsewhere. §2.3.4 ¶1: "Các dấu ấn được đề xuất gồm tăng NT-proBNP, tăng lực tận cùng sóng P ở chuyển đạo V1 và giãn đường kính nhĩ trái." §2.3.4 ¶4: "Nồng độ NT-proBNP vượt ngưỡng 250–400 pg/mL gợi ý quá tải nhĩ..." §2.4.2 ¶3: "bệnh cơ nhĩ với NT-proBNP cao, nhĩ trái giãn và lực tận cùng sóng P bất thường". Also §1.3.3 and §4.1.1.
redundancies.recommendation: Consolidate into §2.3.4 ¶1 with the operational threshold attached there (NT-proBNP >250 pg/mL, PTFV1 >5000 µV·ms, LA diameter index), then delete the triad from §2.4.2 and cross-reference.

redundancies.what: Cancer-associated hypercoagulability with elevated D-dimer and multi-territory lesions is stated twice within a page. §2.3.4 ¶4: "D-dimer tăng cao kéo dài... gợi ý huyết khối liên quan ung thư và là chỉ định tầm soát ung thư tích cực ở người bệnh ESUS có tổn thương đa ổ qua nhiều vùng cấp máu." §2.4.2 ¶3: "tăng đông liên quan ung thư với D-dimer cao và tổn thương đa ổ qua nhiều vùng cấp máu".
redundancies.recommendation: Delete the §2.4.2 clause and expand the §2.3.4 statement into the missing cancer-stroke workup subsection (see gaps) — currently the topic is mentioned twice and developed zero times.

redundancies.what: Hart's high-risk cardioembolic source list appears twice in Chương 2 plus once in Bảng 1.4. §2.3.4 ¶3: "huyết khối thất trái sau nhồi máu cơ tim hoặc trên nền bệnh cơ tim giãn với phân suất tống máu dưới 30%, van cơ học, viêm nội tâm mạc nhiễm khuẩn có sùi van, u nhầy nhĩ trái..." §2.4.2 ¶1: "không có nguồn lấp mạch tim nguy cơ cao như rung nhĩ kéo dài, phân suất tống máu dưới 30%, huyết khối thất trái, van cơ học hoặc viêm nội tâm mạc".
redundancies.recommendation: Keep the full Hart high-/medium-risk taxonomy once, in §2.3.4, ideally as a two-column table (nguy cơ cao / nguy cơ trung bình–thấp) — which the chapter currently lacks despite naming both categories in prose. Replace the §2.4.2 list with "(xem Mục 2.3.4)".

redundancies.what: The chapter closes three separate subsections with the same epistemic disclaimer. §2.1.3: "không thang điểm nào thay thế hoàn toàn được đánh giá tổng thể gồm bệnh sử, khám thần kinh, chẩn đoán hình ảnh và đánh giá tim mạch đa phương thức." §2.2.4: "...chẩn đoán TIA và đột quỵ nhẹ là kết quả tích hợp lâm sàng – hình ảnh, không dựa vào một phương tiện đơn độc." §2.5.3: "...bảng phân biệt chỉ nên dùng để hệ thống hoá việc hỏi bệnh chứ không thay thế đánh giá chuyên khoa."
redundancies.recommendation: Padding. Keep one instance (§2.5.3, where it is most load-bearing) and cut the other two closing sentences; roughly 60 words of pure filler.

redundancies.what: The 2009 tissue-based definitional shift and the reclassification rule are restated in §2.2.1 ¶1 and again in ¶3 ("Khi có tổn thương khuếch tán cấp, người bệnh được phân loại lại thành đột quỵ thiếu máu não nhẹ theo định nghĩa dựa trên mô, kể cả khi triệu chứng đã hồi phục hoàn toàn trong vòng 24 giờ"), after the same point has already been made in ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ ¶2, §1.1.1, Bảng 1.1 (two rows) and §1.1.3(i).
redundancies.recommendation: Open §2.2.1 directly with the imaging question, not with a fourth recapitulation of the definition. Cut ¶1 to one clause and delete the reclassification sentence from ¶3 (Bảng 1.1 already tabulates it).

redundancies.what: §2.5.3 ¶1 restates the row headings of Bảng 2.6 which sits immediately above it: "Bốn nguyên tắc hỗ trợ phân biệt gồm tốc độ khởi phát, tính chất âm hay dương của triệu chứng, phân bố theo vùng cấp máu và bằng chứng cận lâm sàng" — these are exactly rows 2, 3, 4 and 8 of the table.
redundancies.recommendation: Delete the enumerating sentence and keep only its genuinely additive second half (the caveats: migraine can produce negative symptoms, seizure can leave weakness, TIA can produce positive symptoms).

redundancies.what: Bảng 2.4 (AF detection yields) is partly re-tabulated in Bảng 4.4: rows "Phát hiện rung nhĩ | CRYSTAL-AF, EMBRACE | 2014" and "Phát hiện rung nhĩ | STROKE-AF | 2021".
redundancies.recommendation: Acceptable only if §4.3's framing sentence ("ở đây chỉ trình bày bảng tổng hợp") is honoured — but Bảng 4.4's cells restate findings rather than pointing back. Add explicit back-references ("xem Bảng 2.4") to the three monitoring rows of Bảng 4.4.

redundancies.what: The CTA-vs-MRA selection rule is given three times in §2.2: §2.2.3 ¶1 ("Chụp mạch cắt lớp vi tính hoặc chụp mạch cộng hưởng từ xác định hẹp động mạch cảnh ngoài sọ, hẹp nội sọ, tắc mạch và bóc tách"), Bảng 2.3 rows 4–5, and §2.2.4 ¶1 ("lựa chọn giữa chụp mạch cắt lớp vi tính và chụp mạch cộng hưởng từ đầu – cổ tuỳ theo cơ chế nghi ngờ và tính sẵn có").
redundancies.recommendation: Delete §2.2.4 ¶1 entirely — it is a summary of §2.2 misplaced under a Vietnam-specific heading and opens with "Tóm lại" under a new heading. Start §2.2.4 at the three-tier protocol paragraph, which is the only original content there.

inconsistencies.what: Bảng 2.1 labels all three risk strata as 7-day stroke risk — "Nguy cơ thấp | 0–3 điểm: đột quỵ 7 ngày khoảng 1,2%", "Nguy cơ trung bình | 4–5 điểm: đột quỵ 7 ngày khoảng 4,1%", "Nguy cơ cao | 6–7 điểm: đột quỵ 7 ngày khoảng 8,1%" — but 4,1% and 8,1% are the 2-day figures from Johnston 2007, not the 7-day figures; only 1,2% is a 7-day value. The three numbers as printed do not come from a single time horizon. The preceding sentence in §2.1.2 correctly says the score stratifies at "2, 7 và 90 ngày", so the table also fails to deliver what the text promises.
inconsistencies.locations: Bảng 2.1, rows 8–10 (lines 231–233) vs §2.1.2 ¶1 (line 221); compare Bảng 1.3 row "ABCD2 ≥ 4 | Nguy cơ 90 ngày 8–11% so với 1–3%"
inconsistencies.resolution: Restructure Bảng 2.1 into two panels: components (A/B/C/D1/D2, total 0–7) and a risk panel with three explicit columns — 2 ngày / 7 ngày / 90 ngày — populated with the values of the corresponding stratum from Johnston 2007, each anchored to [9]. Verify every value against the source before resubmission; an examiner who knows the ABCD2 paper will check this table first.

inconsistencies.what: §2.4.1 states large-artery atherosclerosis is 15–25% of ischaemic strokes, while §2.4.4 states intracranial atherosclerosis alone accounts for "30–50% số ca nhồi máu não" in East Asia. A subset cannot exceed its parent category. The two statements sit two paragraphs apart in the same section with no reconciliation.
inconsistencies.locations: §2.4.1 ¶2 (line 322) vs §2.4.4 (line 344); the same tension exists between Bảng 1.5 row 2 ("15–25% ngoài sọ; 30–50% nội sọ, Đông Á") and §1.3.4
inconsistencies.resolution: Make explicit that the 30–50% figure is the prevalence of intracranial stenosis (any degree, symptomatic or incidental) among Asian ischaemic-stroke patients in CICAS, not the TOAST large-artery subtype share; and that when intracranial stenosis is the attributed cause, the TOAST large-artery subtype in East Asian cohorts rises to roughly a third. State both denominators in the same sentence.

inconsistencies.what: The TOAST subtype percentages in §2.4.1 sum to 90–115% and conflict with Bảng 1.5. §2.4.1: large-artery 15–25%, cardioembolic 20–30%, small-vessel ~25%, other determined ~5%, cryptogenic 25–30%. Bảng 1.5: cardioembolic 20–25%, small-vessel 20–25%, "lấp mạch chưa rõ nguồn" 15–25% (a different category from "chưa rõ nguyên nhân").
inconsistencies.resolution: Harmonise one set of denominators across the monograph and state whether they are from population-based cohorts or hospital registries. Bảng 1.5 must also stop substituting ESUS for the TOAST "undetermined" category — they are not the same set, as §2.4.2 and §4.1.1 themselves state (ESUS = 50–80% of undetermined).

inconsistencies.what: Cardioembolic proportion is 20–30% in §2.3.1 ("Khoảng 20–30% số ca nhồi máu não và một tỷ lệ đáng kể trường hợp TIA có nguồn gốc lấp mạch từ tim") and 20–30% in §2.4.1, but 20–25% in Bảng 1.5 — and §1.4.1 attributes 20–25% of all ischaemic strokes to atrial fibrillation alone. Taken together, AF would exhaust the entire cardioembolic category, contradicting §2.3.4's list of ventricular thrombus, mechanical valves, endocarditis, myxoma and Libman-Sacks.
inconsistencies.resolution: Fix AF at roughly half to two-thirds of the cardioembolic group and state the total consistently. Cite the same source for the same quantity in all four places.

inconsistencies.what: §2.3.1 asserts "rung nhĩ tiềm ẩn chiếm phần lớn các trường hợp đột quỵ chưa rõ nguyên nhân". This contradicts §2.3.2 (ICM yield 30% at 36 months in CRYSTAL-AF — a minority, and only after three years), §2.3.4 (ARCADIA negative), §2.4.2 (AF listed as one of six occult mechanisms to hunt) and §4.1.2/Bảng 4.1 (four anticoagulation trials neutral in ESUS, the direct empirical refutation of the claim).
inconsistencies.resolution: Rewrite to: occult AF is the single most actionable occult mechanism but is found in a minority — approximately 12% at 12 months and 30% at 36 months with continuous monitoring — and the neutral ESUS anticoagulation trials show that most ESUS is not AF-driven. This is also the intellectual bridge to §4.1.3 and should be written as such.

inconsistencies.what: Three different stenosis thresholds are given for prolonging DAPT in symptomatic intracranial stenosis. §2.4.4: "cân nhắc sớm kháng kết tập tiểu cầu kép cường độ cao khi hẹp nội sọ có triệu chứng" (any degree). §3.2.2: "chỉ dành cho chỉ định riêng như hẹp động mạch nội sọ 70–99% có triệu chứng". ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ ¶4: "hẹp động mạch nội sọ nặng có triệu chứng". §3.2.3 introduces a fourth variant for ticagrelor: "hẹp động mạch cùng bên từ 50% trở lên".
inconsistencies.resolution: Adopt the SAMMPRIS-derived 70–99% threshold for 90-day DAPT everywhere and reserve the ≥50% threshold for the separate ticagrelor indication, naming the trial behind each. Also drop "kháng kết tập tiểu cầu kép cường độ cao" — DAPT has no intensity grading; "cường độ cao" belongs to statin therapy and its use here is a terminology error.

inconsistencies.what: The ABCD3-I imaging item is described generically as any ipsilateral artery. §2.1.2: "hẹp từ 50% trở lên ở động mạch cùng bên trên chụp mạch cộng hưởng từ hoặc cắt lớp vi tính cộng 2 điểm"; Bảng 2.2: "Hình ảnh — mạch máu | Hẹp ≥ 50% động mạch cùng bên | 2". The derived and validated item in Merwick 2010 is ipsilateral carotid stenosis ≥50%. Separately, Bảng 2.2 omits the zero-point options that Bảng 2.1 retains ("khác | 0", "dưới 10 phút | 0"), so as printed Bảng 2.2 cannot generate a score below 2 and the two scoring tables are not parallel.
inconsistencies.locations: §2.1.2 ¶2 (line 235), Bảng 2.2 rows 4–5 and 9 (lines 239–246) vs Bảng 2.1 rows 4–5 (lines 226–227)
inconsistencies.resolution: Restore "động mạch cảnh cùng bên" in both places, restore the 0-point options to Bảng 2.2, and note in the text that ABCD3-I was validated with carotid imaging — applying it to intracranial stenosis (the dominant lesion in Vietnamese patients) is an extrapolation. That caveat is directly relevant to the candidate's thesis and is currently absent.

inconsistencies.what: The same quantity is expressed in two different registers within the chapter: §2.2.1 "Khoảng một phần ba đến một nửa trường hợp TIA theo định nghĩa thời gian có thể có tổn thương khuếch tán", while Bảng 2.6, Bảng 1.1, ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ and §1.1.1 all use "30–50%".
inconsistencies.locations: §2.2.1 ¶2 (line 262) vs Bảng 2.6 row 7 (line 359), Bảng 1.1 row 6, ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ ¶2, §1.1.1 ¶2
inconsistencies.resolution: Use "30–50%" consistently and attach it to the same citation every time.

inconsistencies.what: The range "30–50%" is used for four unrelated quantities across the monograph without any signposting: DWI positivity in time-defined TIA (§2.2.1, Bảng 2.6), minor stroke as a share of admitted ischaemic strokes (ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ, §1.2.1), intracranial atherosclerosis in East Asia (§2.4.4, §1.3.4), and mimics among transient neurological presentations (§2.5.1: "Các bệnh cảnh giả TIA chiếm 30–50% số người bệnh nhập cấp cứu").
inconsistencies.resolution: Tighten at least two of these to the primary sources' point estimates with confidence intervals so the reader can tell the four quantities apart. A reviewer encountering the same range four times will suspect the numbers were not checked.

inconsistencies.what: Terminology drift for "mimic" within one section: §2.5 heading "các bệnh cảnh giả cơn thiếu máu não thoáng qua"; §2.5.1 body "bệnh cảnh giả TIA"; §2.5.2 heading "Các nguyên nhân giả đột quỵ khác" but its body says "Các nguyên nhân giả TIA quan trọng khác"; §2.2.1 uses "nguyên nhân giả đột quỵ"; §2.2.2 uses "bệnh cảnh giả đột quỵ"; §3.1.1 uses "bệnh cảnh giả đột quỵ".
inconsistencies.resolution: Fix one Vietnamese term — "bệnh cảnh giả đột quỵ (stroke mimic)" with "bệnh cảnh giả TIA" reserved for the transient subset — define it once at first use with the English in parentheses, and add it to DANH MỤC CÁC CHỮ VIẾT TẮT or a glossary.

inconsistencies.what: DWI is rendered three ways inside two adjacent subsections: "cộng hưởng từ khuếch tán", "chuỗi xung khuếch tán", "chuỗi khuếch tán"; ADC is "bản đồ hệ số khuếch tán biểu kiến" then simply "hệ số này". Bảng 2.3 uses a fourth form ("Cộng hưởng từ khuếch tán" as a modality name, alongside a separate row "FLAIR, SWI, T2*" that mixes sequence acronyms untranslated).
inconsistencies.resolution: Standardise: "chuỗi xung khuếch tán (DWI)" at first use, "DWI" thereafter; "bản đồ hệ số khuếch tán biểu kiến (ADC)" then "ADC". Add DWI, ADC, FLAIR, SWI, CTA, MRA, TOF, HR-VWI, TCD to the abbreviations table, which currently lists scores and classifications but no imaging acronyms.

inconsistencies.what: The implantable cardiac monitor is called "máy ghi nhịp cấy dưới da" and "máy cấy dưới da" interchangeably within the same paragraph and in Bảng 2.4; the external recorder is "máy ghi biến cố tim ngoài cơ thể" in the table but "máy ghi biến cố tim 30 ngày" in §2.3.1. "Miếng dán ghi điện tâm đồ" is introduced in Bảng 2.4 without definition.
inconsistencies.resolution: Fix one term per device with the English in parentheses at first use, and add ICM/ELR/patch to the abbreviations table.

inconsistencies.what: Bảng 2.3 assigns DWI a fixed sensitivity of "85–95% trong 24 giờ đầu" and NCCT "Dưới 30% trong 24 giờ đầu", while the surrounding text repeatedly warns that DWI is insensitive early and in the posterior circulation, and while §2.2.3 explicitly rejects the practice of quoting fixed sensitivity ranges ("không nên áp dụng các khoảng độ nhạy cố định cho mọi đoạn mạch"). The table thus does exactly what the text forbids two paragraphs later.
inconsistencies.resolution: Either qualify the table values by territory and time from onset (add a footnote: sensitivity falls to ~50–60% for posterior-circulation lesions imaged within 6 hours) or replace the point range with a qualitative rating. Also attach a specific reference to each sensitivity cell; the caption's blanket [5,18,61,62] does not tell the reader where 85–95% comes from.

inconsistencies.what: Hình 2.4's caption states the ICM allows "theo dõi nhịp liên tục trong 3–5 năm", a device-longevity claim supported nowhere in the text and citing [66] (CRYSTAL-AF), which followed patients to 36 months. Reference [69] — the only implantable-monitor device paper in the list (BIOMONITOR III) — is never cited anywhere in the monograph.
inconsistencies.resolution: Cite [69] for the device-longevity statement, or delete the claim. An uncited technical specification in a figure caption is the kind of detail a defence committee picks up.

inconsistencies.what: §2.1.1 gives an inter-arm systolic difference threshold of >20 mmHg ("Chênh lệch huyết áp tâm thu hai tay vượt quá 20 mmHg gợi ý hẹp gốc động mạch dưới đòn hoặc bóc tách động mạch chủ") citing [18,54], neither of which is a source for that threshold; the widely used cut-offs are ≥15 mmHg for clinically significant difference and ≥10 mmHg when screening for subclavian stenosis/steal.
inconsistencies.resolution: State the threshold used, cite it properly, and connect it to the subclavian steal / haemodynamic TIA material that the chapter is missing (see gaps) — otherwise the sentence is an orphan physical-examination fact.

inconsistencies.what: "TIA nguy cơ cao" is used throughout Chương 2 without ever being operationally defined, while §2.1.3 simultaneously forbids using ABCD2 as the sole classifier — yet Chương 3 then defines high risk purely by ABCD2 ("ABCD2 từ 4 trở lên" in §3.1.1/§3.2.2 and "ABCD2 từ 6 trở lên" in §3.2.3). The chapter that is supposed to establish the diagnostic categories never fixes the one category on which all of Chương 3 depends.
inconsistencies.locations: §2.1.3 (line 252) vs §3.1.1 (line 372), §3.2.2 (line 396), §3.2.3 (line 400); term used at §2.1.3, §2.4.2 and throughout Ch.3
inconsistencies.resolution: Add an explicit boxed definition at the end of §2.1.3: high-risk TIA = ABCD2 ≥4 OR crescendo/recurrent TIA OR DWI-positive OR ipsilateral stenosis ≥50% OR cardioembolic source — and say plainly that the trials used the score alone whereas practice uses the composite. Resolving this tension explicitly is one of the strongest things the candidate can do for the mark.

inconsistencies.what: §2.2.4 is headed "Quy trình hình ảnh khả thi cho cơ sở tại Việt Nam" but its first paragraph is a general summary of §2.2 beginning "Tóm lại, hình ảnh não và mạch máu cần hoàn thành càng sớm càng tốt..." with no Vietnamese content, and its final paragraph reverts to generic international principle. Only the middle paragraph (three tiers) matches the heading.
inconsistencies.resolution: Move the "Tóm lại" paragraph to the end of §2.2.3, delete the closing generic paragraph's last clause, and expand the three-tier protocol with the Vietnamese specifics the heading promises (see gaps).

gaps.missingTopic: Cơn thần kinh khu trú thoáng qua trong bệnh mạch máu não nhiễm bột (transient focal neurological episodes of cerebral amyloid angiopathy) — the dangerous TIA mimic
gaps.whyItMatters: This is the single most consequential omission in the chapter. §2.2.2 mentions amyloid angiopathy in one subordinate clause ("có giá trị trong chẩn đoán bệnh mạch máu não thoái hoá dạng bột") and never returns to it; the term appears exactly once in 661 lines. Yet the chapter's whole logic funnels every "high-risk TIA" into DAPT within 24 hours (§2.1.4, §2.4.4) and, if AF is found, into anticoagulation (§2.3.4) — precisely the two decisions that convert a CAA amyloid spell into a fatal lobar haemorrhage. TFNEs are stereotyped, recurrent, spreading positive sensory or negative motor phenomena lasting minutes, associated with cortical superficial siderosis and convexity subarachnoid haemorrhage on SWI, with a ~50% risk of symptomatic lobar ICH within 2 years — the mirror image of the recurrence risk the chapter uses to justify urgent antithrombotics. An examiner in stroke neurology will ask about this. The chapter also never mentions cortical superficial siderosis in its SWI paragraph, never states the Boston criteria v2.0, and never gives a microbleed threshold at which antithrombotic decisions change.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §2.5.5 "Cơn thần kinh khu trú thoáng qua và bệnh mạch máu não nhiễm bột"; plus two sentences in §2.2.2 adding cortical superficial siderosis and convexity SAH to the SWI list; plus a new column or row in Bảng 2.6

gaps.missingTopic: TIA huyết động và cơn run chi (limb-shaking TIA), hội chứng cướp máu dưới đòn, dự trữ vận mạch
gaps.whyItMatters: Directly load-bearing for this candidate's thesis on large-vessel occlusion superimposed on chronic stenosis. Limb-shaking TIA is regularly misdiagnosed as focal seizure and treated with antiepileptics; postural, post-prandial or exertional triggers, symptoms on standing or after antihypertensives, and borderzone (watershed) infarct patterns on DWI are the diagnostic signature of a haemodynamically failing chronically stenosed artery — the exact population the thesis studies. The chapter alludes to triggers in §2.1.1 ("thay đổi tư thế đột ngột, gắng sức, thuốc hạ áp") and lists "dự trữ vận mạch" as a TCD indication in Bảng 2.3, but never explains either concept, never mentions the breath-holding index or acetazolamide challenge, never describes the watershed infarct pattern, and never draws the crucial management inference that in haemodynamic TIA lowering blood pressure is harmful. The §2.1.1 inter-arm blood pressure sentence is left orphaned for the same reason.
gaps.whereToAdd: New subsection under §2.1 (e.g. §2.1.6 "Cơn thiếu máu não thoáng qua do cơ chế huyết động"), with the vasomotor-reserve technique explained in §2.2.3 where Bảng 2.3 already promises it

gaps.missingTopic: Hội chứng cảnh báo bao trong (capsular warning syndrome) và hội chứng cảnh báo cầu não
gaps.whyItMatters: A stereotyped crescendo of purely motor lacunar TIAs carrying a 40–60% risk of completed capsular infarction within 72 hours — the highest short-term risk of any TIA presentation, and one where standard risk scores perform worst because the events are brief and often score low. The chapter counts recurrent TIAs only as a 2-point ABCD3-I item (§2.1.2) and mentions "cơn tái diễn" as an admission trigger (§3.1.3), but never names the syndrome, never states its risk, and never says that these patients must be admitted regardless of score. Fisher's five lacunar syndromes are described in Chương 1 (§1.3.5) but the warning syndrome that is their acute presentation is absent.
gaps.whereToAdd: §2.1.5 (territorial syndromes), immediately after the small-vessel material; add a row to Bảng 1.3 or a cross-reference

gaps.missingTopic: TIA võng mạc, mù thoáng qua một mắt và xử trí tắc động mạch trung tâm võng mạc
gaps.whyItMatters: "Mù thoáng qua một mắt" is invoked three times in Chương 2 (§2.1.1, §2.1.5) and once in Chương 1 as a defining component of the tissue-based TIA definition, yet the chapter contains no fundoscopy instruction, no mention of Hollenhorst plaque, no discussion of the ipsilateral carotid yield in retinal versus hemispheric TIA (retinal events have lower recurrence but similar carotid yield), and — most importantly — nothing on central retinal artery occlusion. Current AHA guidance treats CRAO as an acute ischaemic stroke of the eye requiring the full urgent stroke pathway. The chapter also omits giant cell arteritis screening in patients over 50 with transient monocular visual loss, even though §2.5.3 already lists ESR/CRP for systemic vasculitis; missing GCA means missing a preventable bilateral blindness.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §2.1.7 or a dedicated block within §2.5; add a mimic row to Bảng 2.6 (GCA, ocular causes: vitreous haemorrhage, retinal detachment, papilloedema-related transient obscurations)

gaps.missingTopic: Bảng chi tiết 11 mục thang điểm NIHSS và thang điểm Rankin sửa đổi
gaps.whyItMatters: The whole monograph turns on NIHSS thresholds (≤3 versus ≤5 in ĐẶT VẤN ĐỀ, §1.1.2, §2.1.4, §3.1.2, §3.2.2, Bảng 3.2, Bảng 3.3) and on which low-scoring items are nevertheless disabling (§1.1.2, §2.1.4 both list hemianopia, aphasia, neglect, dominant-hand weakness) — yet the instrument itself is never tabulated. §2.1.1 names it in half a sentence. A diagnosis chapter that adopts a scale as its central classifier must display it. Equally, "tàn tật" is the operative criterion in §2.1.4 but the modified Rankin Scale is never defined anywhere in the document (0 hits for "Rankin" and "mRS" in 661 lines), leaving the key term unanchored.
gaps.whereToAdd: §2.1.1, as a new Bảng 2.1 (11 items with score ranges and a marked column for items whose weight understates disability), renumbering the existing tables; mRS 0–6 as a short second table or an inset

gaps.missingTopic: Hạn chế của ABCD2 ở tuần hoàn sau
gaps.whyItMatters: ABCD2's clinical item scores 2 for unilateral weakness and 1 for speech disturbance and 0 for everything else — so isolated vertigo, diplopia, ataxia or bilateral visual loss from a critically stenosed basilar or vertebral artery scores 0 on the item that carries the most weight. A vertebrobasilar crescendo TIA can therefore score 0–2 and be classified "low risk", which is exactly the failure mode §2.1.3 warns about in the abstract without ever naming the territory where it occurs. This matters disproportionately in Vietnamese practice given the intracranial/posterior predominance the monograph itself emphasises in §2.4.4, and it connects §2.1.3 to §2.5.4 (HINTS, posterior-circulation false-negative DWI), which currently sit unlinked.
gaps.whereToAdd: §2.1.3, as a dedicated paragraph after the ESO/AHA caution

gaps.missingTopic: Xét nghiệm tăng đông và đột quỵ liên quan ung thư
gaps.whyItMatters: The chapter gives one negative instruction ("Xét nghiệm tăng đông không nên thực hiện như một bộ xét nghiệm thường quy cho mọi người bệnh trẻ") and one D-dimer sentence, then stops — the reader is told what not to do but never what to do. Missing: the actual panel; the timing traps the text alludes to but never specifies (antiphospholipid antibodies require confirmation at 12 weeks; lupus anticoagulant is uninterpretable on anticoagulant; protein C, protein S and antithrombin are falsely low in the acute phase and on warfarin/heparin); JAK2 V617F for myeloproliferative disease; PNH flow cytometry; and the Trousseau phenotype — multi-territory DWI lesions with markedly raised D-dimer and no cardiac source — with its distinct management implication that low-molecular-weight heparin, not a DOAC or antiplatelet, is preferred. Also missing: what cancer screening actually means in practice (targeted history plus CT chest/abdomen/pelvis versus age-appropriate screening only).
gaps.whereToAdd: New §2.4.5 "Xét nghiệm tăng đông, hội chứng kháng phospholipid và đột quỵ liên quan ung thư", with a table of test / when to order / when the result is uninterpretable / when to repeat

gaps.missingTopic: Quy trình chẩn đoán đột quỵ và TIA ở người trẻ
gaps.whyItMatters: Chương 1 notes that Vietnamese stroke patients are younger than in high-income countries (§1.2.4) and that dissection is a leading cause under 55 (§1.3.5), but Chương 2 has no young-patient diagnostic pathway at all. Missing: dedicated dissection imaging (fat-saturated T1 neck MRI, not just CTA); RCVS and its thunderclap-headache trigger history; primary and secondary CNS vasculitis; monogenic causes (CADASIL — defined in the abbreviations table and mentioned only once, in §1.4.2 — Fabry disease, MELAS); substance use, including methamphetamine, which is the epidemiologically relevant agent in Vietnam and is not mentioned anywhere; oral contraceptives and hormone therapy (elicited in §2.1.1 but never worked up); and the infectious causes that matter specifically in Vietnam — tuberculous meningitis with vasculitis, neurosyphilis, HIV vasculopathy, varicella-zoster vasculopathy. Rheumatic mitral stenosis, still prevalent in Vietnam, is named only as a DOAC contraindication in Chương 3 and never as a diagnostic target.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §2.4.6 "Tiếp cận chẩn đoán ở người bệnh trẻ tuổi", with a tiered investigation table

gaps.missingTopic: TIA và đột quỵ nhẹ ở phụ nữ mang thai và thời kỳ hậu sản; huyết khối tĩnh mạch não
gaps.whyItMatters: Entirely absent (0 hits for "mang thai"). Two distinct gaps converge here. First, pregnancy and the puerperium change every step of the chapter's algorithm: imaging safety (MRI without gadolinium as the modality of choice, CT dose and abdominal shielding), the differential (eclampsia and PRES, postpartum angiopathy/RCVS, amniotic fluid embolism), and the workup. Second, cerebral venous thrombosis is not mentioned once in the entire monograph despite being a classic cause of transient focal deficits with seizures and headache, requiring a venographic sequence that appears in none of the imaging protocols (§2.2.2, Bảng 2.3, §2.2.4) — and it is precisely the diagnosis in which anticoagulation, not antiplatelet therapy, is indicated even with haemorrhage. Its absence from a differential-diagnosis section is a straightforward examiner target.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §2.5.6 for CVT as a mimic (plus MRV/CTV rows in Bảng 2.3 and §2.2.2), and a pregnancy block either there or as §2.4.7

gaps.missingTopic: Biến cố xảy ra trong khi đang dùng kháng kết tập tiểu cầu — quy trình đánh giá lại chẩn đoán
gaps.whyItMatters: §3.2.4 gives the correct instruction in one sentence ("Khi có tái phát trong lúc đang điều trị, trước khi đổi thuốc cần xác nhận lại mức độ tuân thủ, chẩn đoán, cơ chế bệnh sinh, tương tác thuốc và mức độ hẹp mạch") but the diagnostic work this implies is never specified, and it lives in the treatment chapter rather than the diagnostic one. A breakthrough event is first and foremost a diagnostic event: re-image (has the stenosis progressed? is this now haemodynamic failure? is it in fact CAA or a mimic?), re-classify the mechanism, check CYP2C19 status, and check adherence — before any drug is switched. Given the thesis topic, progression of chronic stenosis to occlusion under antiplatelet therapy is the central clinical scenario and deserves an explicit diagnostic algorithm.
gaps.whereToAdd: §2.4 as a closing subsection ("Đánh giá lại khi biến cố tái phát trong lúc đang điều trị"), cross-referenced from §3.2.4

gaps.missingTopic: Bảng liều thuốc kháng đông đường uống trực tiếp và hiệu chỉnh theo chức năng thận; thuốc đảo ngược tác dụng
gaps.whyItMatters: §2.3.4 asserts that DOAC dose "phải được điều chỉnh theo tuổi, cân nặng, chức năng thận và tương tác thuốc" and §3.4.1 repeats it, but no dosing table exists anywhere in the monograph: no creatinine-clearance cut-offs, no dose-reduction criteria for apixaban (two of three: age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL), no rivaroxaban 15 mg for CrCl 15–50, no edoxaban reduction rules, and — critically — no lower-limit CrCl at which each agent is contraindicated. Reversal agents are absent from the entire document (0 hits for idarucizumab, andexanet, "đảo ngược"), even though §3.4.3's pre-initiation checklist and the whole early-anticoagulation discussion (§3.4.2, ELAN/OPTIMAS/CATALYST) presuppose a plan for haemorrhagic complications. "Độ thanh thải" appears nowhere. For a monograph claiming to be a practical Vietnamese guide this is a conspicuous hole.
gaps.whereToAdd: The table itself belongs in §3.4.1 (Bảng 3.6b) with reversal agents in §3.4.3; in Chương 2 the fix is to delete the half-statement in §2.3.4 and cross-refer

gaps.missingTopic: Chi phí – hiệu quả của mô hình phòng khám TIA
gaps.whyItMatters: The 80% risk reduction is asserted five times but its economics never once, even though reference [31] (Luengo-Fernandez, the long-term cost analysis of EXPRESS) is already in the list and cited elsewhere. For a monograph whose stated purpose is to "đề xuất quy trình khả thi cho điều kiện Việt Nam", the argument that will actually persuade a hospital director is that urgent evaluation reduces total cost through avoided bed-days and avoided disabling strokes — EXPRESS showed benefit "không tăng chi phí" (§1.2.2 says so in passing and never develops it). Cost per QALY, the bed-day arithmetic, and a sensitivity analysis under Vietnamese unit costs would convert a literature review into an implementation case.
gaps.whereToAdd: §2.5.4 or, better, a new closing §2.6 for the service-delivery material

gaps.missingTopic: Chỉ số chất lượng (KPI) của quy trình chẩn đoán TIA
gaps.whyItMatters: Absent entirely. A doctoral monograph that proposes a diagnostic pathway must say how the pathway will be measured: proportion assessed by a specialist within 24 hours, door-to-imaging time, proportion receiving DWI, proportion with head-and-neck vascular imaging before discharge, proportion with 12-lead ECG plus appropriate rhythm monitoring, mimic rate, proportion started on secondary prevention on the same day, 90-day recurrence, and a defect-free composite. Vietnam already participates in the RES-Q registry (cited as [34] in §1.2.4), so the measurement infrastructure exists and the link is available for free. This is also what makes the chapter auditable rather than merely descriptive.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §2.6 "Chỉ số chất lượng và triển khai quy trình chẩn đoán", with a KPI table (indicator / numerator / denominator / target / data source)

gaps.missingTopic: Giáo dục người bệnh, tư vấn lái xe và trở lại công việc
gaps.whyItMatters: Zero mentions of driving in the whole document. At the moment the diagnosis is made, three things must be communicated and documented: recognition of recurrence (FAST/BE-FAST in Vietnamese, and the instruction to call emergency services rather than wait), driving restriction — with reference to the Vietnamese driver health standards (Thông tư liên tịch 24/2015/TTLT-BYT-BGTVT) and the different rules for professional/group-2 licence holders, which is a real medico-legal exposure for the treating physician — and return to work. §2.1.4 twice makes "khả năng trở lại công việc" the operational test of disability, so the chapter already depends on a return-to-work concept it never develops. This is standard content in every TIA guideline and its absence is immediately visible.
gaps.whereToAdd: New §2.6 alongside the service material, or as a closing block of §2.5.4

gaps.missingTopic: Quy trình TIA từ xa (telemedicine / tele-TIA)
gaps.whyItMatters: "Từ xa" appears only inside the caption of Hình 1.2 (a foreign RESCUE-TIA workflow) and in §4.4.2's AI discussion; Chương 2 contains no telemedicine pathway. This is the single most practical answer to the problem the monograph itself identifies — that stroke resources in Vietnam are unevenly distributed and concentrated on severe stroke (§1.2.4) — and Vietnam has a national framework for it (Đề án Khám chữa bệnh từ xa, Quyết định 2628/QĐ-BYT năm 2020) plus an established hub-and-spoke stroke network. What belongs here: which decisions can safely be made remotely (triage, NIHSS by video, image review) and which cannot; DICOM transfer requirements, which §2.2.4 already gestures at ("nên gửi dữ liệu DICOM thay vì ảnh chụp màn hình") without building a pathway around it; and the tele-TIA clinic as a substitute for the physical rapid-access clinic in provinces without 24/7 MRI.
gaps.whereToAdd: §2.2.4 (integrated into the three-tier protocol) and §2.6

gaps.missingTopic: Chi tiết triển khai đặc thù Việt Nam
gaps.whyItMatters: §2.2.4 is the chapter's only Vietnam-specific block and is generic enough to apply to any middle-income country.
